heading: EXT. CARNIVAL OF DUST, ABANDONED PRAIRIE FAIRGROUND - DUSK

units.text: EXT. CARNIVAL OF DUST, ABANDONED PRAIRIE FAIRGROUND - DUSK
A rusted Ferris wheel stands against a bruised orange sky, its gondolas swaying and groaning.
Wind rolls tumbleweeds between the empty tents.
A torn banner snaps: "GRAND JUBILEE."
EZEKIEL TOLLIVER, fifties, in a long black coat and a battered hat, sits on a barrel by the shooting gallery, a revolver across his knee.
SORREL McCREA, thirties, in a split riding skirt and a man's vest, stands twenty paces away with her thumbs hooked in her belt.
JUBAL CREED, young, nervous, crouches behind a barrel with a rifle.
You've come a long way, Sorrel.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Not as long as you.
units.name: SORREL

units.text: It never is.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: The wheel groans.
A gondola swings loose and clangs against its frame.
Jubal flinches and the rifle barrel rises an inch.
Tell your boy to put it down.
units.name: SORREL

units.text: Jubal. Put it down.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Mr. Tolliver, I
units.name: JUBAL

units.text: Down.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Jubal lowers the rifle.
Dust blows between them.
In the silence, a distant bell chimes from the abandoned chapel, three notes.
PEARL, a girl of twelve in a patched dress, steps out from behind the tilt-a-whirl with a bucket of water in each hand.
She sees the three of them, stops, and sets down the buckets without a sound.
Ezekiel's eyes go to her.
Sorrel's hand opens at her side.
Pearl. Go back.
units.name: SORREL

units.text: Pearl does not move.
